content.title:
Scored quiz
Module 6
content.intro: This quiz covers all the lessons in this module. You must achieve 80% to pass. Good luck!

questions.prompt: What percentage of total global greenhouse gas emissions is attributed to the energy sector?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: The energy sector is responsible for roughly 75% of total global GHG emissions, making it the largest contributor to climate change.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: The energy sector is responsible for roughly 75% of total global GHG emissions, making it the largest contributor to climate change.

questions.prompt: Which of the following greenhouse gases has the highest global warming potential (GWP) among those commonly emitted by the energy sector?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: SF₆ has the highest GWP about 25,200 times that of CO₂ making it a critical target for emission reductions in energy distribution.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: SF₆ has the highest GWP about 25,200 times that of CO₂ making it a critical target for emission reductions in energy distribution.

questions.prompt: What are key environmental impacts associated with the development of renewable energy infrastructure?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: All options are correct. Habitat disruption and land use conflicts arise from large-scale installations, air pollution can occur during material production and decommissioning, and mining for minerals needed in solar panels, wind turbines, and batteries causes serious environmental degradation.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: All options are correct. Habitat disruption and land use conflicts arise from large-scale installations, air pollution can occur during material production and decommissioning, and mining for minerals needed in solar panels, wind turbines, and batteries causes serious environmental degradation.

questions.prompt: How does climate change impact the performance and reliability of energy systems?

options.value: It increases cooling demand during heatwaves, stressing electricity grids
It improves thermal plant efficiency by warming water sources
It disrupts hydropower generation due to changing rainfall patterns
It increases the risk of infrastructure failure from extreme weather events

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Climate change stresses systems by increasing cooling needs, disrupting hydropower, and exposing infrastructure to weather extremes. Warmer water actually reduces—not improves—thermal plant efficiency.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Climate change stresses systems by increasing cooling needs, disrupting hydropower, and exposing infrastructure to weather extremes. Warmer water actually reduces—not improves—thermal plant efficiency.

questions.prompt: What are key challenges limiting the widespread adoption of renewable energy technologies in developing countries?

options.value: High initial capital costs and financing constraints
Lack of technical capacity and skilled labor
Inconsistent policies and weak grid integration

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: All listed options are documented constraints: high costs, skills gaps, market volatility, and policy/infrastructure weaknesses.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: All listed options are documented constraints: high costs, skills gaps, market volatility, and policy/infrastructure weaknesses.

questions.prompt: Which of the following accurately describe lifecycle emissions from energy technologies?

options.value: Lifecycle emissions account for all stages from resource extraction to decommissioning
Solar and wind have significantly lower lifecycle emissions than coal or gas
Natural gas and coal are comparable to wind and solar in lifecycle emissions
Lifecycle emissions are only relevant for fossil fuels

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Lifecycle analysis provides a comprehensive view of emissions. Wind (13g CO₂/kWh) and solar (43g CO₂/kWh) are far lower than coal (1,001g) and natural gas (486g). Lifecycle analysis is relevant for all energy types.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Lifecycle analysis provides a comprehensive view of emissions. Wind (13g CO₂/kWh) and solar (43g CO₂/kWh) are far lower than coal (1,001g) and natural gas (486g). Lifecycle analysis is relevant for all energy types.

questions.prompt: Which sector is the largest contributor to global CO2 emissions from end-use sectors?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Transport is the largest source of end-use CO2 emissions, responsible for over one-third, making it a priority sector for decarbonization through electrification and efficiency improvements.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Transport is the largest source of end-use CO2 emissions, responsible for over one-third, making it a priority sector for decarbonization through electrification and efficiency improvements.

questions.prompt: Why is lifecycle emissions analysis critical for comparing renewable and fossil energy technologies?

options.value: Because it reveals true emissions impacts beyond the point of use
Because it measures only the emissions from fuel combustion
Because renewables can show lower total emissions even after including manufacturing and disposal
Because it’s the only metric governments use to set climate targets

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Lifecycle analysis includes emissions from construction, use, and decommissioning. It highlights how renewables remain lower-emission even when all stages are considered.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Lifecycle analysis includes emissions from construction, use, and decommissioning. It highlights how renewables remain lower-emission even when all stages are considered.
